# Visit Our Sewing Machine Warehouse in Houston, TX

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Who is Sewing and Vacuum Warehouse and where are you located?

A full‑service retail and online store for sewing, quilting, embroidery, longarm, and vacuums with
two locations:
• [13233 N Eldridge Pkwy, Cypress, TX 77429][116]
• [2018 I‑45 North, Suite B, Conroe, TX 77301][117]
Hours: Mon–Fri 10–6, Sat 10–5. Phone: (888) 857‑1746.

### Do you service and repair machines?

Yes—Service & Repairs include in‑store service and a virtual check‑in for machine service.

### 
### What products and brands do you carry?

Sewing/quilting machines, sergers/coverstitch, embroidery (single‑ and multi‑needle), longarm
machines/frames/accessories, sewing furniture, notions/supplies, cutting/printing tools, software,
vacuums, and pre‑owned machines. Featured brands include [Janome][118], [Juki][119], and
[Brother][120] (see Shop By Brand for the full list).

### 
### Do you offer classes and repair services?

Yes. Classes include [sewing/serging][121], [quilting][122], [embroidery][123], [longarm][124],
[ScanNCut][125], [bag making][126], [paper piecing][127], and software, plus virtual events. Full
in‑store service and repairs are available, with online virtual check‑in for machine service.

### Got a Question?

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Who is Sewing and Vacuum Warehouse and where are you located?

A full‑service retail and online store for sewing, quilting, embroidery, longarm, and vacuums with
two locations:
• [13233 N Eldridge Pkwy, Cypress, TX 77429][116]
• [2018 I‑45 North, Suite B, Conroe, TX 77301][117]
Hours: Mon–Fri 10–6, Sat 10–5. Phone: (888) 857‑1746.

### Do you service and repair machines?

Yes—Service & Repairs include in‑store service and a virtual check‑in for machine service.

### 
### What products and brands do you carry?

Sewing/quilting machines, sergers/coverstitch, embroidery (single‑ and multi‑needle), longarm
machines/frames/accessories, sewing furniture, notions/supplies, cutting/printing tools, software,
vacuums, and pre‑owned machines. Featured brands include [Janome][118], [Juki][119], and
[Brother][120] (see Shop By Brand for the full list).

### 
### Do you offer classes and repair services?

Yes. Classes include [sewing/serging][121], [quilting][122], [embroidery][123], [longarm][124],
[ScanNCut][125], [bag making][126], [paper piecing][127], and software, plus virtual events. Full
in‑store service and repairs are available, with online virtual check‑in for machine service.

* ✅ Зарегистрируйтесь и подтвердите e-mail

Управляйте заказами и получайте уведомления через [Telegram-бота][51].

## About the American Textile History Museum

The American Textile History Museum, which was located in Lowell, Massachusetts, was dedicated to
capturing the significance of textiles in America’s cultural and industrial heritage. Established in
1960 and originally part of the Smithsonian Institution, the museum chronicled the American textile
industry from its early domestic beginnings to its transformation into a powerful global force.

Its collections encompassed all aspects of the textile industry, including machinery, artifacts,
photographs, and documents. The museum showcased how textiles were integral to the evolution of
American life, including technological advancements, labor movements, and fashion trends. Key
exhibitions often highlighted the innovations in textile machinery, the role of immigrants in the
industry, and the impact of textiles on everyday life.

Unfortunately, the museum closed in 2016 due to financial difficulties. Despite its closure, its
collections continue to be an important resource for researchers and historians, as they offer a
comprehensive view into the historical tapestry of America’s industrial past. Many of the artifacts
and archives were transferred to other institutions, ensuring that the legacy of the textile
industry and its impact on American history remains accessible and preserved.

## About ATHM

ATHM was founded to continue the legacy of the American Textile History Museum, by providing
educational content around fabrics, textiles, and the history thereof.  We are not affiliated with
the Smithsonian Institute, and are an independent operation.  We hope to provide some value through
our research, editing, and creativity.

#### Bengal Muslin

## Reviving the legend

Our project is dedicated towards the revival of the fabled fabric known as muslin. It commenced in
early 2014, and has successfully revived the story of muslin and its origin in Bangladesh, woven
‘new muslin’ of up to 400 count from cotton plants whose fibre is close to the original ‘*phuti
karpas*’. Bengal Muslim has thus revived the heritage and production of the cloth in Bangladesh.

[ Learn More ][108]

# “Weaving Heritage into the Future: An Exclusive Interview with Saiful Islam, CEO of Bengal Muslin”

## THE REVIVAL

[ View All ][109]

## [Background and Mission][110]

Our goals are; to reveal the true history of the fabric and its connection with our land and
culture; to inspire its revival by researching and implementing the age old processes; to bring
recognition to the ‘lost heroes’ i.e. the artesans, who have retained the tradition.

## [Muslin Cotton][111]

Gossypium Arboreum Var. Neglecta (*phuti karpas*) was the unique cotton plant, short stapled and red
stemmed, that flourished on the banks of the river Meghna from which muslin’s high-count, fine yarn
was woven.

## [Muslin Festival][112]

It was one-of-a-kind festival, with a cultural show, (held at the residence of Dhaka’s Nawab’s,
Ahsan Manzil) and an exhibition, along with a book launch, a seminar and a tour of muslin producing
areas.

## [Muslin Tour][113]

On the 8th February, 2016, a group of textile experts including Rosemary Crill and Sonia Ashmore,
(both researchers from the V & A Museum, UK) were taken on a day long tour of muslin’s historic
areas.

## [Muslin Exhibition][114]

From 5th February 2016, a month-long exhibition, arranged by Drik-Bengal Muslin and attended by over
100,000 visitors, was held at the Bangladesh National Museum.

## Story of Muslin

[ View All ][115]

## [History][116]

Muslin’s history is rich, complex and beyond what is attributed to a simple craft. A cloth so fine
that at various times in recorded history it was described as ‘woven air’ and ‘the skin of the
moon’. The Mughals called it ‘*mul-mul*’. The English traded, exploited and exterminated the cloth.
Its true history is finally being revealed.

#### Bengal Muslin

## Reviving the legend

Our project is dedicated towards the revival of the fabled fabric known as muslin. It commenced in
early 2014, and has successfully revived the story of muslin and its origin in Bangladesh, woven
‘new muslin’ of up to 400 count from cotton plants whose fibre is close to the original ‘*phuti
karpas*’. Bengal Muslim has thus revived the heritage and production of the cloth in Bangladesh.

[ Learn More ][108]

# “Weaving Heritage into the Future: An Exclusive Interview with Saiful Islam, CEO of Bengal Muslin”

## THE REVIVAL

[ View All ][109]

## [Background and Mission][110]

Our goals are; to reveal the true history of the fabric and its connection with our land and
culture; to inspire its revival by researching and implementing the age old processes; to bring
recognition to the ‘lost heroes’ i.e. the artesans, who have retained the tradition.

## [Muslin Cotton][111]

Gossypium Arboreum Var. Neglecta (*phuti karpas*) was the unique cotton plant, short stapled and red
stemmed, that flourished on the banks of the river Meghna from which muslin’s high-count, fine yarn
was woven.

## [Muslin Festival][112]

It was one-of-a-kind festival, with a cultural show, (held at the residence of Dhaka’s Nawab’s,
Ahsan Manzil) and an exhibition, along with a book launch, a seminar and a tour of muslin producing
areas.

## [Muslin Tour][113]

On the 8th February, 2016, a group of textile experts including Rosemary Crill and Sonia Ashmore,
(both researchers from the V & A Museum, UK) were taken on a day long tour of muslin’s historic
areas.

## [Muslin Exhibition][114]

From 5th February 2016, a month-long exhibition, arranged by Drik-Bengal Muslin and attended by over
100,000 visitors, was held at the Bangladesh National Museum.

## Story of Muslin

[ View All ][115]

## [History][116]

Muslin’s history is rich, complex and beyond what is attributed to a simple craft. A cloth so fine
that at various times in recorded history it was described as ‘woven air’ and ‘the skin of the
moon’. The Mughals called it ‘*mul-mul*’. The English traded, exploited and exterminated the cloth.
Its true history is finally being revealed.

## [Process and Techniques][117]

Muslin’s manufacture involved sixteen complex processes which were carried out by different castes,
religion, gender, age and communities of which spinning yarn and weaving the ‘flowered and figured’
(*jamdani*) muslin were the most complex activity and prized product.

## [Today’s ‘Muslin’][118]

The Bengal muslin industry was decimated by the policies of the East India Company. By using the
re-discovered *phuti karpas* cotton (a 70% match), blending and spinning it in India, we have
recreated saris up to 400 count in their original, Mughal era motifs.

## [Muslin Anecdotes][119]

William Bolt wrote in 1770, in his “Consideration on Indian Affairs”, that the Mughal Emperor,
Aurangzeb, once chastised his daughter for being naked although the princess was fully clothed in
seven layers of muslin. Read more such tales in this section.

## [Our achievements so far][120]

We pioneered in researching muslin and published its definitive history; discovered ‘*phuti karpas*‘
cotton with a 70% match; wove 400 count ‘new muslin’ saris and held the Muslin Festival in Dhaka.
Our pioneering efforts have inspired others, with whom we shared our research findings.

## Information of Muslin

[ View All ][121]

## [Print Media][122]

In early 2014, Drik commenced a special project on ‘Bengal Muslin’ with the intention of retrieving
its history and process. Since then a large number of publications/news sites, both general and
specialised, have reported on different aspects of this invaluable work.

## [Future plans][123]

It is an art that deserves revival. We continue to inform the world about muslin’s heritage, weave
and promote it’s products and recognise the artesans by improving their financial and working
conditions.

## [Why are we doing this?][124]

Western view on muslin has prevailed till now. Serious research and efforts for its revival were not
done before our project. We believe that this craft deserves to be recognised and supported as
Bangladesh’s heritage.

## Muslin

A delicate fabric that evokes tactile ecstasy. Weightless, light, as if filled with air. So delicate
that it is used to sew clothes for babies. Always in place, always comfortable. It washes well and
doesn't lose its shape. At home, outside in the summer, on vacation - clothes made from muslin
instantly become your favorite.

## Ramie

Made from nettle fibers, Ramie fabric has a thousand-year history and is highly prized. The process
of creating ramie is very labor-intensive and unique, therefore it has the status of an elite
fabric. The main advantages of the fabric are high strength. Ramie will never harbor microorganisms;
it is easy, effective to clean and dries quickly.

**About Flipside Products Inc.
**
Flipside Products Inc. is an educational products manufacturer headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio.
Since 1990, we have manufactured and distributed quality learning tools at prices built for school
budgets. Our Cincinnati operation handles product development, warehousing, and fulfillment for our
network of distributors across North America.

 

**
Frequently Asked Questions**

Who is the manufacturer of Flipside Products?

Flipside Products come from Flipside Products Inc. This company manufactures educational supplies
and classroom products and is located in Cincinnati, Ohio.

Where are Flipside Products made?

Most of our project boards, foam boards, and select dry-erase boards are proudly made in the USA at
our Cincinnati facility. Imported items are clearly marked on the product page.

Are Flipside Products available wholesale?

Yes. We are a school and educational supply distributor providing wholesale classroom supplies, bulk
educational products, and school supplies to schools, districts, and approved resellers.

What types of educational supplies does Flipside manufacture?

We specialize in classroom essentials, including dry-erase boards, whiteboards, tri-fold project
boards, foam-core boards, cork bulletin boards, easels, study carrels, privacy shields, and
certificates.

## trusted by thousands of companies globally

why lemon squeezy?

## global tax compliance, fraud prevention, multi-currency support, failed payment recovery, PayPal
## integration and more. We make running your software business easy peasy.

01

### Global tax compliance

We’re your merchant of record. That means **we handle payments, merchant fees, fraud and sales tax**
without you lifting a finger.

02

### Borderless SaaS payments

Instantly sell your digital products around the globe. As your merchant of record, you can **accept
payments from 135+ countries** right out of the box with zero setup.

03

### Instant payment methods

Our no-code and API solutions **support 20+ payment methods**, and we offer bank payouts globally.

04

### Local currency support

Offer your products in your local currency to **increase checkout conversions**. Lemon Squeezy
currency support spans 130+ countries.

05

## Why it's luxury & how it's a masterpiece?

You can not make dhakai muslin even with the best ai. Muslin needs generational skills, patience &
time. Spinners make 500 thread count yarn with the rarest cotton phuti karpus magical fingers.

Master weavers visualize the design and weave just by intuition & skills that pass through their
ancestors. It takes sixteen steps with almost 20 different people to complete one Dhaka Muslin. The
process follows the same rules from a thousand years ago!

You can not replicate this masterpiece. Can not even produce! Impossible to scale this quiet luxury.

# What is a Muslin Fabric?


Muslin Cotton is a versatile and enduring fabric celebrated for its distinctive breathable weave and
exceptional durability. Dating back to the 13th century, as highlighted by Marco Polo in his
renowned writings, muslin has been valued for its luxurious and refined qualities.

Crafted with a plain weave technique, muslin cotton features a straightforward yet effective pattern
where weft threads interlace with warp threads. This construction results in a lightweight,
breathable fabric ideal for layering. Muslin varies from a soft, fine texture to a more open,
gauze-like weave, depending on its specific construction, and is available in multiple layers or
gauze.

Perfect for a range of uses from delicate garments to practical home textiles, muslin cotton
combines classic elegance with functionality. Explore the timeless charm and versatility of muslin
cotton for your next project or wardrobe addition today. Buy Cotton Muslin Fabrics Online from our

###### ABOUT

### We’re driving meaningful change right from the start of the supply chain.

Most of the materials used for fashion, textile, and apparel today come from farms, forests, or
fossil fuels. Textile Exchange exists to ensure the industry treats these resources with respect.

[Our story][102]
[Get involved][103]
[sustainable textiles cotton farming]

###### WHAT WE DO

## Our purpose is to build a global fiber and materials production model that positively impacts our
## planet

At the heart of our strategy is the goal of helping the fashion, textile, and apparel industry to
reduce the greenhouse gas emissions that come from fiber and raw materials production by 45% by
2030. We call it Climate+.

[Discover Climate+][104]
[soil health HOME][soil health HOME]

##### Soil

Soil puts food on our plates, purifies the water, and is the beginning of all material production.
We’re striving to keep it healthy.

[forest HOME][forest HOME]
[forest.][forest.]

##### Biodiversity

Like food and the air we breathe, material production depends on healthy ecosystems which need a
wide variety of animals, plants, and microorganisms. That’s why we’re supporting biodiversity.

[water moving HOME][water moving HOME]
[water.][water.]

##### Water

The basis of life as we know it, water, needs to be treated as the precious resource it is. We work
to make sure it is used responsibly and put back safely into our systems.

* [ Sustainability Standards ][106]

We help the industry to understand some of the common sustainability challenges that come with
producing popular fibers and raw materials. Then, we work with stakeholders all along the supply
chain to find ways to overcome them at scale.

# Climate action starts at the source of the materials we choose

Watch video [Learn about our mission][101]

###### ABOUT

### We’re driving meaningful change right from the start of the supply chain.

Most of the materials used for fashion, textile, and apparel today come from farms, forests, or
fossil fuels. Textile Exchange exists to ensure the industry treats these resources with respect.

[Our story][102]
[Get involved][103]
[sustainable textiles cotton farming]

###### WHAT WE DO

## Our purpose is to build a global fiber and materials production model that positively impacts our
## planet

At the heart of our strategy is the goal of helping the fashion, textile, and apparel industry to
reduce the greenhouse gas emissions that come from fiber and raw materials production by 45% by
2030. We call it Climate+.

[Discover Climate+][104]
[soil health HOME][soil health HOME]

##### Soil

Soil puts food on our plates, purifies the water, and is the beginning of all material production.
We’re striving to keep it healthy.

[forest HOME][forest HOME]
[forest.][forest.]

##### Biodiversity

Like food and the air we breathe, material production depends on healthy ecosystems which need a
wide variety of animals, plants, and microorganisms. That’s why we’re supporting biodiversity.

[water moving HOME][water moving HOME]
[water.][water.]

##### Water

The basis of life as we know it, water, needs to be treated as the precious resource it is. We work
to make sure it is used responsibly and put back safely into our systems.

### Explore fibers and materials

We help the industry to understand some of the common sustainability challenges that come with
producing popular fibers and raw materials. Then, we work with stakeholders all along the supply
chain to find ways to overcome them at scale.

### Explore sustainability standards

We’ve developed a set of robust standards to give the industry a way to authenticate their
sustainability claims from raw material to final product. They fill the gaps in existing guidelines
and verification tools, and we regularly adapt and upgrade them to meet evolving needs.

# Habillez vos espaces avec des textiles sur mesure créés pour vous

Depuis près d’un demi-siècle, Textiles Patlin transforme les espaces hôteliers en lieux uniques où
confort et élégance se rencontrent. Literie, rideaux et voilages prennent vie grâce à notre
savoir-faire et à la personnalisation de chaque détail, jusqu’à l’impression de designs exclusifs.
Avec notre approche clé en main, nous aidons les hôtels à créer des ambiances inoubliables qui
marquent l’expérience et fidélisent la clientèle.

### Hôtelier

## Nos services de confection
## sur mesure

Rehaussez l’expérience de votre clientèle grâce à un décor exclusif qui vous démarque.

### Habillages de lits sur mesure

**Plus de 36 000 habillages de lits fabriqués sur mesure à notre actif**

Affichez vos couleurs avec nos habillages de lits personnalisés. Couvre-lits, housses de couette,
jupes de lit, couvre-oreillers ou jetés : tout ces articles peuvent être un véhicule pour votre
identité visuelle. Tissus de qualité, designs sur mesure et confection soignée, pour un résultat à
la hauteur de votre établissement.

**Plus de 50 000 habillages de fenêtres fabriqués sur mesure au compteur**

draperies : nous allions les textures pour vous permettre de maîtriser la lumière et rehausser votre
décor. Importation ou impression de tissus, prise de mesures, confection précise et installation
professionnelle : On s’occupe de tout.

# Habillez vos espaces avec des textiles sur mesure créés pour vous

Depuis près d’un demi-siècle, Textiles Patlin transforme les espaces hôteliers en lieux uniques où
confort et élégance se rencontrent. Literie, rideaux et voilages prennent vie grâce à notre
savoir-faire et à la personnalisation de chaque détail, jusqu’à l’impression de designs exclusifs.
Avec notre approche clé en main, nous aidons les hôtels à créer des ambiances inoubliables qui
marquent l’expérience et fidélisent la clientèle.

## Nos services de confection
## sur mesure

Rehaussez l’expérience de votre clientèle grâce à un décor exclusif qui vous démarque.

### Habillages de lits sur mesure

**Plus de 36 000 habillages de lits fabriqués sur mesure à notre actif**

Affichez vos couleurs avec nos habillages de lits personnalisés. Couvre-lits, housses de couette,
jupes de lit, couvre-oreillers ou jetés : tout ces articles peuvent être un véhicule pour votre
identité visuelle. Tissus de qualité, designs sur mesure et confection soignée, pour un résultat à
la hauteur de votre établissement.

[ Je découvre ce service ][51]

### Draperies et rideaux sur mesure

**Plus de 50 000 habillages de fenêtres fabriqués sur mesure au compteur**

Alliez élégance et performance avec nos habillages de fenêtres sur mesure. Rideaux, voiles et
draperies : nous allions les textures pour vous permettre de maîtriser la lumière et rehausser votre
décor. Importation ou impression de tissus, prise de mesures, confection précise et installation
professionnelle : On s’occupe de tout.

[ Je découvre ce service ][52]

### Conception et impression textile

**Donnez vie à vos idées et personnalisez votre décor!**

De l’inspiration à la création, nous concevons et imprimons vos motifs sur mesure pour tous vos
projets d’aménagement. Grâce à l’impression numérique textile, tout devient possible : vos couleurs,
vos textures et vos détails… sur le tissu de votre choix.

## About Us

Since her days of studying Fashion Entrepreneurship at NIFT (Delhi), a question that has hounded our
founder Richa Maskara Agrawal is, what does *sustainability in fashion* really mean?

Steeped in a culture of giving back, and a vision for a sustainable future, Richa spent years on
researching the process of fabric making before founding The Muslin Shop.

Her belief in the importance of the right fabric was deepened when she became a mother herself.

Childhood being too short to wear boring clothes, The Muslin Shop’s products are designed with style
and comfort occupying top priority and kids tested and approved (literally!) to bring forth some
snuggly, fun and sustainably made clothes and baby products.

## About Us

founder Richa Maskara Agrawal is, what does *sustainability in fashion* really mean?

researching the process of fabric making before founding The Muslin Shop.

Childhood being too short to wear boring clothes, The Muslin Shop’s products are designed with style
and comfort occupying top priority and kids tested and approved (literally!) to bring forth some
snuggly, fun and sustainably made clothes and baby products.

ABOUT US

# China's Leading Tarpaulin Manufacturer

For over two decades, LINYI TONGYUAN PLASTICS CO., LTD has been at the forefront of tarpaulin
manufacturing in Linyi, China. With advanced production technology and a commitment to quality,
we've built a reputation that spans across more than 120 countries worldwide.

Our comprehensive product range includes PE tarpaulin, PVC tarpaulin, canvas tarpaulin, [HDPE
tarpaulin][43], and custom solutions tailored to your specific requirements. Whether you need
waterproof covers for agriculture, heavy-duty truck tarps, or industrial-grade protection, we
deliver products that exceed expectations.

As a trusted B2B partner, we combine competitive pricing with uncompromising quality, making us the
preferred choice for wholesalers, distributors, and procurement managers across the globe.

[Learn More About Us →][44]

Why Choose Us

## Why Buyers Choose TONGYUAN

Factory-direct manufacturing, stable quality control, and flexible customization for global B2B
tarpaulin buyers.

### Factory-Direct Pricing

No trading company markup. Transparent pricing based on material, GSM, size, and order volume.

### Full Customization

Customize GSM, widths, colors, printing, eyelets, reinforced edges, and export packaging.

### Stable Quality Control

Every batch is checked for GSM, tensile strength, UV performance, and dimensional accuracy.

### Real Factory Capacity

12 production lines support stable bulk supply for distributors, importers, and industrial buyers.

### Export Experience

20+ years serving global markets with FOB Qingdao terms and complete export documentation.

### Direct Communication

Work directly with our export team for fast answers, production updates, and clear accountability.

## Our values

Quality

In our company, we value every detail of the production process of our textiles. From the choice of
natural fibres to the final finish, we pay special attention to the quality of touch, softness and
warmth of our products.

We control every stage of the production process in our facilities 100%. In this way, we can
guarantee that each garment that carries our stamp is unique and sustainable, with a quality that
can be felt and seen in every fibre.

Innovation and technology

In our production process, we use state-of-the-art technology and machinery to develop innovative
collections. Our aim is to achieve greater efficiency and effectiveness in order to obtain maximum
profitability, maintaining this policy in all areas of our activity.

Cooperation

We generate synergies with companies in the sector, always thinking of contributing and adding
positive experiences to our customers.

We are committed to working together with our partners to offer the best of us, to ensure a
satisfactory and enriching experience for everyone.

Flexibility

As manufacturers and distributors we adapt to the needs of each customer, controlling all the
production processes (spinning, weaving and finishing).

Sustainability

We are a socially and environmentally certified textile industry by SMETA, which guarantees the
quality, ecology and sustainability of our textiles. We also have the Global Recycled Standard and
Oeko Tex certificates, which contribute to saving energy and sustaining a circular economy.

## Textiles to create modern and stylish homes

[ About us ][20]

##### We weave your dreams

## Unique and sustainable textiles for home and decoration

## More than 50 years of experience in the textile industry

We manufacture and distribute textile articles for the home with the aim of creating cosy
atmospheres. We want to offer you products that not only fill every corner with warmth, but also
contribute to creating a better world.

[ About Us ][21]

## Our values

Quality

In our company, we value every detail of the production process of our textiles. From the choice of
natural fibres to the final finish, we pay special attention to the quality of touch, softness and
warmth of our products.

We control every stage of the production process in our facilities 100%. In this way, we can
guarantee that each garment that carries our stamp is unique and sustainable, with a quality that
can be felt and seen in every fibre.

Innovation and technology

In our production process, we use state-of-the-art technology and machinery to develop innovative
collections. Our aim is to achieve greater efficiency and effectiveness in order to obtain maximum
profitability, maintaining this policy in all areas of our activity.

Cooperation

We generate synergies with companies in the sector, always thinking of contributing and adding
positive experiences to our customers.

We are committed to working together with our partners to offer the best of us, to ensure a
satisfactory and enriching experience for everyone.

Flexibility

As manufacturers and distributors we adapt to the needs of each customer, controlling all the
production processes (spinning, weaving and finishing).

Sustainability

We are a socially and environmentally certified textile industry by SMETA, which guarantees the
quality, ecology and sustainability of our textiles. We also have the Global Recycled Standard and
Oeko Tex certificates, which contribute to saving energy and sustaining a circular economy.
